## Product variant uniqueness review correction

Final review found a concrete WP-1020 invariant missing from the new creation
path: variant selections form a set, but hashing request order could admit two
SKUs with the same Dimension/Value pairs in reverse order. Canonicalize transport
variant order and compute owner uniqueness/digest from sorted Dimension references;
reject duplicate combinations before writes. Preserve operation snapshot content
and avoid changing shared legacy domain parsers. Add the reversed-pair HTTP case
and rerun only the affected creation database scenario plus changed types/lint.
BFF28 gate evidence is unchanged and reusable; no schema or other journey rerun.

## Ordinary refund confirmed-position reducer

Payment owns a deterministic internal projection over a complete persisted
observation history and the recovered original dispatch/request. Reconstruct
each observation against that original binding, reject conflicting identities
or terminal evidence, and count one individual succeeded refund once.
Failure, cumulative snapshots, pending, canceled and failed observations do not
prove safe release. Unknown observations after success do not erase confirmation.
This step does not expose a route, change SQL, enable release, or wire balances.

Payment owns an immutable Requested record containing scoped requester/reason,

installed by this step. Future append-only outcome records must explicitly
govern release; ordinary and compensation readers must be composed before use.

## Refund allocation preserves released unit positions

Before persistence, replace contiguous-only quantity input with explicit occupied
unit ordinals. For each original line unit j, component entitlement is
floor(component*j/quantity)-floor(component*(j-1)/quantity). Select lowest free
ordinals; return them for claim persistence. A proven no-effect release frees
only that claim's original ordinals. Other claims keep the same cents, even when
a gap opens. Unknown/confirmed ordinals stay occupied. Algorithm V1 is not yet
published or persisted; this refines its initial in-progress implementation.

## Pricing ordinary refund allocation RF-D05

Algorithm ORDINARY_REFUND_ALLOCATION_V1: immutable source ref/digest and original
CAD net/item-tax per line; original tip/service-charge/service-charge-tax totals.
Allocate each order-level component once using existing allocateMoney largest
remainders, original net weights and stable uppercase item-reference keys.
Zero-net lines have zero weight when any net exists; when all net is zero use
original quantity weights. Allocate cumulative quantity entitlement with integer
floor(component * cumulativeQty / originalQty); this request is new minus prior
entitlement. Residual cents thus reach final quantities; never recompute weights
from the remaining lines. Caller supplies already-occupied quantities under
Payment/Ordering fences and must reconcile earlier allocation version/digest.
No manual override or Provider authority. Selection: affected Pricing lint/build,
new allocation behavior tests including permutation, zero amounts, partial/full
conservation and invalid quantity/money; reuse unchanged allocateMoney evidence.

## Dining commitment implementation slice

Dining owns a closed immutable checkout commitment tied to Session/Table assignment, active
Participant, Guest, Cart/version, Quote, submission, Order/Batch and permanent Payment operation.
Implement its prepared-to-payment-pending lifecycle first in
packages/rms/dining/src/domain/dining-checkout-commitment.ts, export through src/index.ts, and
exercise src/tests/dining-checkout-commitment.test.ts. No Ordering or Payment private dependency.
Preparation uses a bounded source-validity instant, not a fabricated Pickup Hold. Sealing requires
the exact live Session and Participant versions plus acknowledged Ordering linkage; its immutable
original request instant determines exactly 30 minutes. Expiry returns only the commitment fact,
never a Table, Session, other Batch or financial transition. Replay cannot renew either deadline.
These pure functions are not authorization or persistence; owner transaction/Audit, current Guest
authority, closure/move serialization and actual PostgreSQL evidence remain required next.

## Payment preparation dependency resolution, 2026-09-10

The next producer must reconcile the existing public contracts before activation.
PaymentIntentCreationPorts.ordering.preparePayment accepts a tipSelectionReference (nullable)
and requestedAt. Its service binds that selection reference into the operation intent digest;
it requires capacityExpiresAt to equal requestedAt plus exactly 30 minutes. Consequently the
API must supply Dining's persisted original paymentRequestedAt, not a new request-arrival time.
An original sealed clock is history and does not establish current eligibility.

Existing immutable OrderCreationRecord.items[].pricing.total supplies the original Order
allocation amount. Sum Money using bigint and validate exact original Order/Batch/Quote scope;
do not reprice a committed Order or substitute the current Cart total. Payment's existing
1400_001 table persists tip_minor in the immutable PaymentIntent, but the inspected Payment and
Ordering application sources provide no tip-selection producer or lookup for the preparation
port. The new preparation composition must not turn an unresolved selection into a zero tip.

Authority: accepted Section 27.7 separates optional tip from item prices; Section 28.5 assigns
tip to each PaymentIntent/Transaction and excludes it from Order unpaid-balance reservation.
Section 87 requires selection before confirmation and immutable Money snapshots. The locally
readable source matches these requirements at lines 2134-2137, 2225-2233 and 21262. This is source
reconciliation, not acceptance of a new full Handoff baseline or tax/legal/provider fixture.

## Customer submission HTTP boundary — resolved next integration

Current-state inspection: customer-pwa checkout-client.ts implements loadCart/quote only;
REST catalog.ts has no customer Order submission endpoint; API has internal Dining/Pickup
submission compositions but no customer Order handler. The previous internal PostgreSQL passes
therefore do not prove browser submission. CUST-CHECKOUT is Phase 1 /checkout, Guest plus exact
Store/journey scoped, and CUST-ORDER-STATUS uses /orders/{orderReference} (Section 88.6).
No visual redesign or Figma mutation is planned.

Next bounded transport implementation:

- POST /api/v1/orders, idempotency-key is the permanent submission UUIDv7. Closed JSON body:
  cartReference, cartVersion, quoteReference. Server resolves Guest channel/Store and chooses
  Dining/Pickup composition; never accept caller Brand/Store/Actor or authoritative amounts.
- Existing secure Guest cookie, x-csrf-token, same-origin Origin/Fetch-Metadata, JSON limits,
  no-store/no-referrer, bounded request handling and standard safe errors remain required.
- Call only the existing create operation. Tip must still be selected explicitly before clock
  sealing; this endpoint neither calls a Provider nor implies payment eligibility or success.
- Project a closed customer-safe result from the parsed original Order: original Order reference
  and number, submission/Cart/version/Quote binding, orderType, Submitted/NotReported and exact
  original total. No Guest identity, Catalog/Option policy evidence, capacity internals, credentials
  or private request payload in response/logs. Validate returned binding before sending.
- Created => 201, original AlreadyCreated => 200; permission/not-found => nondisclosing 404;
  request malformed => 400; version/idempotency conflict => 409; invalid/requote-needed selection
  => 422; unavailable/uncertain => 503 and retry the same submission. Never renew identity on timeout.
- Implement apps/api/src/customer-order-submission.ts and its tests, route it through app.ts with
  default unavailable behavior unless the owning port is supplied, and update REST catalog/tests/
  generated contract. Connect actual Dining/Pickup submission ports; reuse existing isolated

Authority: accepted Section 30.3, 30.6-30.8; existing InventoryUnit, NegativeStockPolicy and
StockBalanceSnapshot. This calculator consumes already base-unit quantities, preserves inTransit,
derives available = onHand - reserved, enforces exact ledger precision and an expected balance
version, and returns an immutable next snapshot. It never rounds silently or chooses workflow timing.
Release/ConsumeReserved cannot exceed aggregate reserved quantity. The future owner transaction
must additionally bind the exact reservation/scope, authorize, serialize the balance/version,
append Movement/Audit/idempotent result and preserve original-operation recovery.

Insufficient on-hand/available returns an explicit required control from the supplied existing
Block/ManagerOverride/AllowWithWarning policy; no boolean override or pure calculation is financial/
inventory admission. Override requires authorization plus an exception/task; warning requires an
exception/task. The calculator does not produce StockMovementFact, approval, final checkout
evidence or persistence and does not infer SKU-to-Item conversion, Lot selection or Store policy.

### Inventory reservation calculation evidence

Added calculateReservationBalance in the existing Inventory owner. Reserve changes reserved only;
Release returns held quantity without adding on-hand; ConsumeReserved reduces on-hand and reserved
together; ConsumeUnreserved does not release another reservation. All quantities use scaled BigInt,
normalize decimal output and honor the explicit base unit's ledger precision without rounding.
Inputs are closed data records, balances must satisfy available = onHand - reserved, expected version
must match and the next version must be representable. Reserved/in-transit cannot be negative;
Release/ConsumeReserved cannot exceed total reserved quantity. Output snapshots are immutable.

Negative resulting on-hand/available returns Block, ManagerOverrideAndExceptionRequired, or
ExceptionRequired according to explicit existing policy. None is arithmetic-only, not authorization.
No override boolean, workflow default, SKU mapping, stock scope/lot inference, movement, permission,
reservation identity or successful stock/persistence fact is manufactured. Exact reservation
ownership, production-start release restrictions, current Item/Store policy and transactional
concurrency remain the next owner lifecycle/application work.

## Inventory reservation lifecycle

Continue Section 30.3/30.6 within the existing Inventory owner, without schema activation.
Add domain/inventory-reservation.ts, public export and focused tests under packages/rms/inventory/src.
The immutable versioned reservation binds Tenant/Brand/Store/Stock Site/Location/Item/Lot plus
Cart/version, Quote, submission and exact owner-supplied demand reference/digest. Store its explicit
base unit and original quantity; remaining + released + consumed must equal that original exactly.
Partial Release/Consume never exceed this reservation's remaining quantity, even when aggregate
stock reserved contains other reservations. Production-start is irreversible; Release after it is
denied, leaving Consume/Waste handling to the approved owner workflow. No automatic release timeout,
automatic production start or Consume timing is chosen.

Each transition checks the full binding, expected reservation version and monotonic UTC instant,
returns a new frozen snapshot and preserves prior snapshots. Pure lifecycle does not authorize,
validate current Item/Lot/workflow, resolve durable idempotency, create Audit/Movement, or claim
database concurrency. The application will use the previous balance calculator and persist both
reservation/ledger changes atomically after current authority. No negative override, stock policy
default, allocation/mapping source or dependency is invented. Same focused Inventory test/lint/tsc
and format/boundary checks apply; unchanged calculator tests run alongside lifecycle because the

### Inventory reservation lifecycle evidence

Added createInventoryReservation / parseInventoryReservation / advanceInventoryReservation.
Snapshots bind the exact reservation reference plus all named stock/submission/demand fields;
canonical closed parsing rejects accessors and scope drift. Original, remaining, released and
consumed base-unit quantities are exact and conserved. Version-1 snapshots cannot claim prior
activity. Partial lifecycle operations preserve original identity/unit/quantity, enforce monotonic
time and version bounds, and return frozen new snapshots. StartProduction never changes quantity;

an owner-directed transition without assuming a Store workflow trigger. Terminal zero-remaining
reservations cannot consume/release again.

### Atomic multi-account reservation primitive

Extend the existing Inventory store with reserveAll: one caller transaction for all reserve
children, common submission/cart/quote/demand/time/actor binding, distinct accounts/operations/
reservations, deterministic Item/account order, and original output order. Reuse each existing
commit's current Item/hold/balance/Audit fences and idempotent history. Any later child failure
rolls back earlier child writes; reject a mixed existing/new result instead of accepting a partial
prior operation set. This is a low-level atomic primitive, not a durable batch identity: the
complete expected child set must still be sealed by the final submission/demand owner. No claim
that replay of a smaller all-existing set verifies original batch completeness. No new schema.
Test actual second-account failure rollback and successful all-child retry using existing DB case.

### Workflow-to-Publishing snapshot binding

Bind a publication to the immutable Draft immediately preceding its Published Workflow version.
Publishing family is workflowReference; snapshotReference is that Draft versionReference and its
snapshotDigest is RFC8785/SHA256 of the complete normalized Draft. Use technical metadata codes
WORKFLOW_DEFINITION / WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION, not inferred business-purpose conversions. Confirm
Draft/Published content equality except lifecycle/version/publication metadata already allowed by
the Workflow writer. The Workflow owner reads its own original Draft, then the Publishing public
current-source port validates release and approval IDs plus exact snapshot and scope in the same
transaction. Missing, changed, superseded or archived releases fail. Store override authorization
remains a separate gate; a Brand release alone does not authorize a Store override.

### Ordering current-state Payment fence implemented

Ordering query store exposes withCurrentSubmission on the caller transaction, acquiring a
scoped order_header FOR UPDATE lock through the submission link before decoding current owner
facts. It never marks the outer transaction read-only. Missing header skips callback; invalid
current initial-state history fails closed. Existing read-only resolveSubmission is unchanged.

API customer-order-payment-admission.ts binds exact Order/Batch/Cart/version/Quote/guest and
creation time, then delegates the finite capacity/Inventory admission result while retaining
the header lock. Composed helper grants only UPDATE(order_id) needed for the scoped test role's
row lock, asserts another connection cannot lock the Order at Payment INSERT, and rejects a
mismatched Order before Inventory timing evaluation. No cancellation writer or policy added.

### Intact-reservation rule implementation and evidence

Inventory exports evaluateIntactReservationPaymentRule. It strictly parses final Inventory,
current Item snapshots and reservations, requires exact complete/nonduplicate sets, current
scope/unit/tracking/version/time coherence and intact original reservation quantities.
Deferred does not satisfy this named rule; NotTracked and ZeroDemand may satisfy their exact
validated disposition. This is explicitly selected prerequisite evaluation, not a blanket
reserve-before-pay decision or a replacement for lot/expiry/access/capacity checks.
